To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the coalescent can be constructed by adding edges between roots; this new representation allows to make numerous connections with other combinatioral and probabilistic models, such as size biased percolations, parking schemes in trees, increasing trees, and random cuts of trees; the new construction allows us to derive a new combinatorial identity, a new combinatoric interpretation of the coalescent, and a new combinatorical proof of the coalescence property.

(i) the coalescent forests can be represented as the increasing trees of the parking scheme, (ii) the coalescence of roots in the forest representation corresponds to the size biased percolated clusters in the parking scheme, and (iii) the number of clusters in the forest representation is the number of trees in the parking scheme.

the block sizes in the parking scheme in a rooted tree, the cluster sizes of size-biased percolation, and the sizes of increasing trees, are all distributed according to the same law as the cluster sizes in the additive coalescents.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following three questions. 1. What is the probability that a random node of a coalescent forest is a root? 2. How many roots are in a random coalescent forest? 3. How many roots can we find in a coalescent tree?
the following question: how does the additive coalescence behave when edges are added between roots instead of adding them between nodes?
the following questions: What are the combinatorial properties of these new objects? What is the probability distribution of the number of roots at a given time?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the additive coalescence process can be represented as a random process on the set of increasing trees.
the additive coalescents can be seen as a random process which is both a coalescent of trees and a fragmentation of trees, in a sense that is made more precise in the paper.
the coalescent process can be viewed as a process of random cuts of a tree.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the additive coalescents are a family of Markov processes which have many different combinatorial representations.
we have discovered an interesting combinatorial model, the parking scheme in a forest, and we have found its connection with the coalescent process.
, for the additive coalescence starting from n particles, we have found a new combinatorial model which has the same law as the classical model, but is more tractable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the additive coalescence process can be viewed as a random process of rooted forests.
the additive coalescence process, which is usually considered in the literature as a process of forests, is actually a process of rooted trees.
the additive coalescence can be seen as a coalescence between trees.
